findings.summary: A personal WhatsApp mobile number is hardcoded in client-side source and permanently published on a public GitHub Pages site and in git history.
findings.failure_scenario: Any visitor, bot, or scraper who views the page source or the deployed site can read WHATSAPP_NUMBER (redacted) from index.html and the rendered chat button/link. The page has no access control, and once a commit is pushed the number also remains recoverable from git history even if a later edit swaps it out, so it should be treated as permanently public.
findings.recommendation: Use a dedicated shared/team WhatsApp Business number for IT support instead of a personal mobile number, since anything committed to a public repository's source or history is effectively public forever. Resolved: WHATSAPP_NUMBER cleared to a blank config placeholder and the value purged from git history via a full history rewrite.

findings.summary: No Content-Security-Policy is set for the page.
findings.failure_scenario: If a future edit accidentally introduces an XSS gap (e.g., a raw innerHTML assignment with unescaped input, bypassing the existing escapeHtml() helper), there is currently no CSP to limit script execution as a defense-in-depth backstop.
findings.recommendation: Consider adding a restrictive <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; connect-src https://formsubmit.co"> tag, since the page is fully self-contained and only needs to reach formsubmit.co over the network.
